questions.prompt: Is there a defect in how this code validates the incoming trigger request? If so, mark the line(s) where it is; otherwise answer that there is none.
A client sends a well-formed JSON object whose "priority" is the string "high". What does decodeTrigger return?
choices: A 422 response listing the priority field, because validate() finds it is not between 0 and 9
A 400 response with a field error for "priority" saying the type is wrong, produced during decoding before validate() runs
A request with Priority left nil, because the decoder skips values it cannot convert
A 400 response with an empty Fields list, because every decoding error is reported as malformed JSON

questions.prompt: A request body is {"branch":"main"} followed by a second object {"branch":"dev"} in the same body. What happens?
choices: Both objects are decoded and the last one wins
The first object is accepted and the rest of the body is ignored
The request is rejected with 400 because the decoder finds more data after the first value
The request is rejected with 413 because the body exceeds maxBodyBytes

questions.prompt: Which statement about the variables check is correct?
choices: Per-variable checks run for every request regardless of how many variables are supplied, so a request with thousands of variables produces thousands of field errors
Names starting with "CI_" are accepted as long as they match the name regex
Value length is counted in bytes, so a 4096-character value of multi-byte characters is rejected
When more than 50 variables are supplied, only a single "variables" error is produced and the per-variable loop is skipped
